name: survival-guard-confirmation
question: The factorial says the survival guard raises score by +0.184 [-0.021, +0.381] and lowers self-kills by -0.044 [-0.087, +0.000] over 18 checkpoints and 120 worlds. Under its registered rule that is a DO NOT SHIP, because the self-kill interval had to clear zero and its upper bound landed exactly on zero. The rule stands and we are not reinterpreting it. What is still open is a different question: on Monday we must hand in one of these two agents, and we would like to hand in the better one. This run asks that question on worlds neither variant has seen and on the newest checkpoints we have.
relationship_to_the_factorial: That experiment answered whether the guard's benefit is established. This one is a choice between two variants of our own agent. We keep the two apart on purpose: the scientific claim stays 'not established' whatever happens here, and this result may only decide which artifact we package.

power.estimated_before_running: We resampled the factorial's own per-checkpoint, per-world differences to imitate this design. If the true effect is the observed +0.184, a rule demanding the 95% interval clear zero would succeed about 35% of the time here, and only about 48% even with 24 checkpoints and 200 worlds over seven hours.
power.why: The guard's effect varies more between checkpoints (sd 0.267) than the effect itself is large (0.184), and we only have a handful of checkpoints. More worlds barely help, because the checkpoint level dominates and we cannot manufacture more replicas in time.
power.consequence: A significance test we would fail on a coin flip cannot decide anything, and running one and then reading it loosely is exactly the trap we want to avoid. So the rule below is a decision rule under uncertainty, fixed in advance, and the interval is reported rather than used as a gate.

design.why_only_two: The factorial already showed the two factors are additive and that neither alone is detectable (bomb -0.036, move -0.024, both -0.044 on self-kills, interaction +0.016). There is nothing left to decompose, so every game here goes into the comparison we would actually act on.
design.agent: Bomb-omb-survivalguard, the same prototype, unchanged since commit ecc58bb

checkpoints.judged: the 12 milestones at episodes 6,000 and 8,000: control-r1..r3 and halved-r1..r3 at each
checkpoints.why_these: They are the two newest levels we have, so they are the closest thing to the checkpoint we will actually ship, and 12 checkpoints is the most the laptop can carry in an afternoon. The factorial found no decay across episodes 2,000 to 6,000, so if the guard helps at 8,000 as well, applying it to a much later checkpoint is a short step rather than a leap.
checkpoints.also_played: the untrained reference, for context only. It does not enter the decision.

suite.name: survival-guard-confirmation-fresh
suite.seed_audit: We checked all 250 seeds and their plus and minus 1,000,000 offsets against every integer of six digits or more in the 940 readable tracked text files on 18 September. No collision, no overlap with the held-out suite, and no overlap with the factorial worlds (980000001-120), the classic monitoring worlds (970000001-100) or the loop-guard worlds (960000001-100). Neither variant has played any of these boards.

decision_rule.type: decision under uncertainty, not a significance test
decision_rule.contrast: both minus control, paired on the same checkpoint and the same world

interval.method: hierarchical paired bootstrap, resampling the 12 checkpoints and then the 250 worlds

ship_if_all: the score point estimate is at least 0
the lower bound of the score interval is above -0.15, so a real cost is ruled out even though a real gain is not established
the self-kill point estimate is at most 0, so the guard does not make the thing it was built for worse
decision_rule.otherwise: Bomb-omb ships exactly as trained, and the guard becomes a negative result in the report.
decision_rule.what_we_will_not_claim: Whatever this run shows, we will not write that the guard significantly improves the agent. If it ships, it ships as the better of two options on the evidence we could afford, and the report says so in those words.
reported_without_gating: the 95% interval for score and for self-kills, and whether either clears zero
the split by episode 6,000 versus 8,000, to see whether the benefit survives at the newest level
how many of the 12 checkpoints improved

known_limits: Opponents are not seeded, so part of every difference is noise that pairing cannot remove.
Twelve checkpoints from six training seeds is a small sample of a noisy population, and six of them were also judged in the factorial. The worlds are fresh, the checkpoints only partly.
We will ship a checkpoint near episode 24,000 and judge here at 6,000 and 8,000.

A decision rule that ships on a non-negative point estimate will sometimes ship something useless. We accept that: the cost of shipping a neutral guard is small, and the factorial already ruled out a large loss.
expected_cost: 2 cells x 13 checkpoints x 250 worlds = 6,500 games, about 4 to 5 hours with two jobs.
authorization: Julius (1BlauNitrox) asked for this confirmation on 18 September 2026 after reading the factorial.
